You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
What must equal marginal cost when a profit-maximising firm produces at its allocatively efficient output?

options.C: total revenue
options.D: total cost

questions.questionText: What might reduce dynamic efficiency in an economy?

options.C: rising shareholder dividends
options.D: the increase in innovation

questions.questionText: In many countries, health authorities are concerned about the harmful effects of smoking cigarettes. Governments have imposed high sales taxes on cigarettes and have conducted anti-smoking campaigns. Why might the quantity of cigarettes demanded remain high?

options.A: Better knowledge of health hazards is changing behaviour.
options.B: Cigarette smoking will be replaced by cheaper alternatives.
options.C: Consumer behaviour is irrational due to addiction.
options.D: The income effect of a price rise makes consumers worse off.

questions.questionText: What does a budget line show?

options.A: the behaviour of a utility-maximising consumer
options.B: the difference between an individual’s consumption and saving
options.C: the monetary value of the disposable income of a consumer
options.D: the maximum combinations of two products that a consumer can buy with a given level of income

questions.questionText: When the price of a good falls, the overall effect on the quantity demanded can be separated into income and substitution effects. Which statement describes a Giffen good?

options.A: The income effect is irrelevant for a Giffen good.
options.B: The income effect works in the same direction as the substitution effect.
options.C: The income effect works against the substitution effect and is of a greater magnitude.
options.D: The income effect works against the substitution effect but is of a smaller magnitude.

questions.questionText: The table provides some details of the soft drinks industry in a country. number of firms 250 number of brands 1000

A rock band is due to play at a concert hall. In order to create a good atmosphere, the band’s aim is to sell all the tickets. Ticket prices are set at the highest price that ensures all tickets will be sold. What is the motivation for this price strategy?

options.C: sales maximisation
options.D: satisficing

questions.questionText: What would be most likely to allow the survival of small firms in an economy?

options.A: an increase in the cost of borrowing from commercial banks
options.B: an increase in personal services as a share of GDP
options.C: an increase in the rate of change of information technology
options.D: an increase in the ratio of capital to labour employed in an economy

questions.questionText: What is a condition for operating a successful cartel?

options.A: a large number of firms in the industry
options.C: low barriers of entry to the industry
options.D: strictly enforced production quotas

questions.questionText: In 2012, an Australian airline company separated its international and domestic operations into separate companies. The company had been facing increasing competition from much larger competitors in international markets but had relatively little competition in domestic markets that had a higher price elasticity of demand. Which row shows the reasons that would support this separation? diseconomies of scale the level of markets can easily in the combined competition and be separated by company before the price elasticity in this company separation domestic markets

options.C: yes yes no
options.D: yes yes yes

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s marginal and average cost curves. The firm enters a collusive agreement with other firms in the industry. It is agreed that each firm will charge a common price, OP, and will restrict the level of its output to a production quota set by the industry cartel. The firm is allocated a production quota, Oq. price MC AC G H P K L J M N O q quantity The firm decides to cheat in order to maximise its profits. What is its short-run increase in profits?

options.C: PHJL minus PGNM
options.D: PGKL minus LKNM

questions.questionText: To reduce road congestion caused by parked cars, a local government introduced a system of tradable parking permits. Households were given a permit allowing them to park one car at the roadside. Households with more than one car could buy extra permits from households with no cars. What is the most likely reason for this policy to fail?

options.A: Fines for drivers parking in the area without a permit will internalise the externality.
options.B: The local government has a monopoly over the issue of parking permits.
options.C: Those suffering from too many parked cars are compensated by the households owning extra cars.
options.D: Too many households own cars so the market in permits is very small.

questions.questionText: What is not an example of the application of ‘nudge’ theory?

options.A: A chain of coffee shops offers its customers a larger coffee if they bring their own reusable cup.
options.B: A government imposes an indirect tax on the purchase of sugary snacks, to try to reduce childhood obesity.
options.C: A government introduces an opt-out system for organ donation, to try to increase the number of organs donated.
options.D: A restaurant chain introduces smaller-sized main courses on its menu, to try to reduce the volume of food wastage.

questions.questionText: A government wishes to redistribute income from richer citizens to poorer citizens. Which policy is it least likely to use?

options.C: increase subsidies
options.D: increase transfer payments

questions.questionText: What represents the transfer earnings of the factor enterprise?

options.C: return on capital
options.D: start-up costs

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand for and supply of labour in the construction industry. The labour market is initially in equilibrium when the wage is W .

options.A: trade union wishes to increase the wage but does not wish to decrease employment. The union asks for wage W . The employers offer wage W .

questions.questionText: Many governments adopt sustainable economic growth as a macroeconomic policy aim. What is meant by sustainable economic growth?

options.A: increasing the current productive potential of the economy as fast as possible
options.B: increasing the current productive potential of the economy by using only low-cost resources
options.C: increasing the current productive potential of the economy without reducing future productive potential
options.D: increasing the future productive potential of the economy as fast as possible

questions.questionText: What would cause estimates of the money value of the Measure of Economic Welfare for a country to be greater than the value of Gross National Product?

options.C: regrettable necessities
options.D: the value of non-marketed activities and leisure

questions.questionText: The data provides information on indicators of the standard of living in four countries in 2019, each with a population below 10 million. Gross National expected skilled labour life expectancy country Income per capita years of (% of labour at birth (years) ($) schooling force) Croatia 78.3 23061 15.0 91.5 Norway 82.3 68059 18.1 84.3 United Arab Emirates 77.8 66912 13.6 52.8 Qatar 80.1 110489 12.2 43.9 Based (overall) on these indicators, which country is most likely to have had the highest HDI ranking?

options.C: United Arab Emirates
options.D: Qatar

questions.questionText: What might help improve economic growth in developing countries over the next five years?

options.B: an increase in the birth rate
options.C: an increase in the budget surplus
options.D: an increase in training

questions.questionText: An economist once said ‘if you pay people not to work and tax them when they do, don’t be surprised if you get unemployment’. What is this an example of?

options.C: structural unemployment
options.D: voluntary unemployment

questions.questionText: What is the least likely consequence of a significant rise in unemployment during an economic recession?

options.B: a fall in expenditure on welfare
options.C: a fall in revenues from income tax
options.D: a fall in the rate of economic growth

questions.questionText: In which context relevant to growth in the money supply is the term total currency flow used?

options.A: the money flow between central banks and commercial banks
options.B: the money flow between central banks and governments
options.C: the money flow between domestic residents and foreign residents
options.D: the money flow between the general public and the financial sector

questions.questionText: What does not change the level of withdrawals from the circular flow of income?

options.A: households having more of their income taken in tax following a rise in the rate of income tax
options.B: households spending more on imported cars following a currency appreciation
options.C: households taking money from their savings to spend on a celebration
options.D: households transferring money from an account in one bank to a different bank

questions.questionText: Which approach is consistent with the Keynesian school of economic thought?

options.A: Balanced budgets should be a key policy aim.
options.B: Inflation is caused by excessive money supply growth.
options.C: Unemployment can still persist in the long run.
options.D: Wages are flexible downwards in the short run.

questions.questionText: What could be used to offset a leakage from the circular flow of income?

options.C: an increase in the rate of interest
options.D: an increase in investment

questions.questionText: In some countries, life expectancy has fallen but the birth rate remains high. Which effect will this have?

options.A: Fewer schools and other resources for young people will be needed.
options.B: More facilities will be needed for older people.
options.C: There will be an ageing population.
options.D: The working population will tend to become a smaller percentage of the total population.

questions.questionText: The government’s chief economist says that increasing the top rate of income tax from 40% to 45% is likely to reduce tax revenue by 2%. Which economic concept might explain this prediction?

options.C: Lorenz curve
options.D: Phillips curve

questions.questionText: Which combination of policies is most likely to reduce the rate of inflation? government direct taxation interest rates spending on households
